items.claim: CEO cites gross retention of 97-98% across the >11,000-customer installed base as evidence customers are not leaving.
items.quote: a gross retention rate of 97% to 98%.
items.speaker: Carl Eschenbach, CEO

items.claim: CEO states Workday software sits on the desktop of 73 million end users.
items.quote: We are on the desktop of 73 million users, 73 million users.
items.speaker: Carl Eschenbach, CEO

items.claim: CEO states 75% of customers already use AI features bundled into the core platform subscription, without an added AI upcharge.
items.quote: 75% of our customers are using AI that's in the platform
items.speaker: Carl Eschenbach, CEO

items.claim: CEO describes Workday's AI differentiation as building first-party, enterprise-focused domain-specific agents.
items.quote: we're building first-party agents, our own agents
items.speaker: Carl Eschenbach, CEO

items.claim: CEO says Workday has announced 13 first-party AI agents to be showcased at the upcoming user conference.
items.quote: We have 13 of them we've announced.
items.speaker: Carl Eschenbach, CEO

items.claim: CEO frames the Agent System of Record as the orchestration layer for onboarding third-party AI agents like employees.
items.quote: the Agent System of Record as the orchestration layer
items.speaker: Carl Eschenbach, CEO

items.claim: CEO recalls repeated existential threats to VMware from open-source hypervisors that never materialized, drawing a parallel to today's AI-disruption narrative.
items.quote: We were going out of business.
items.speaker: Carl Eschenbach, CEO

items.claim: Discussion references the earlier market debate that AWS would commoditize software as a historical analogue to the current AI-commoditization fear.
items.quote: AWS is going to commoditize software debate
items.speaker: Kasthuri Rangan, Analyst

items.claim: CEO says Workday is model-agnostic and treats LLM providers as interchangeable rather than betting on one winner.
items.quote: they're interchangeable for us from an LLM perspective.
items.speaker: Carl Eschenbach, CEO

items.claim: CEO states Workday has acquired 4 AI companies in the last 1.5 years as part of an inorganic AI build-out.
items.quote: in the last 1.5 years, we bought now 4 AI companies
items.speaker: Carl Eschenbach, CEO

items.claim: CEO confirms the most recent acquisition is Paradox, a conversational AI platform aimed at frontline workers.
items.quote: we announced an acquisition of a company called Paradox
items.speaker: Carl Eschenbach, CEO

items.claim: CEO describes launching a dedicated Workday Government subsidiary to invest in and target the U.S. federal market.
items.quote: we launched actually the Workday Government subsidiary
items.speaker: Carl Eschenbach, CEO

items.claim: CEO acknowledges AI will drive further economies of scale, implying pressure on customer headcount/seat growth even as he disputes it being AI-driven job cuts.
items.quote: AI will drive further economies of scale
items.speaker: Carl Eschenbach, CEO

items.claim: CEO gives an ambiguous, self-qualifying statement on customer headcount growth trend immediately before saying overall headcount still grows.
items.speaker: Carl Eschenbach, CEO

items.claim: CEO says Workday will provide a further update on its AI pricing and monetization strategy at the upcoming Financial Analyst Day.
items.quote: we'll provide a further update on our AI pricing strategy
items.speaker: Carl Eschenbach, CEO

items.claim: CEO states the AI business is growing 100% year-over-year.
items.speaker: Carl Eschenbach, CEO

items.claim: CEO repeatedly defers quantification of the AI book of business to the following week's Financial Analyst Day.
items.speaker: Carl Eschenbach, CEO

items.claim: CEO commits to keeping Flowise, the acquired agent-building platform, open source going forward.
items.quote: we are going to keep an open source platform.
items.speaker: Carl Eschenbach, CEO

qa_flags.question: Analyst asks whether seat-based/headcount growth pressure tied to AI is structural or just a correction from pandemic-era overhiring (noted as the same question asked on the earnings call three weeks earlier).
qa_flags.response_pattern: CEO calls the narrative 'completely overblown', pivots to an anecdote about a Fortune 10 CIO and a TAM-expansion argument rather than giving specific seat/logo growth figures, and gives internally inconsistent phrasing ('It's moderating. It's not growing.') immediately before stating overall customer headcount continues to grow.

qa_flags.question: Analyst asks the CEO to quantify the AI book of business, referencing that peer SaaS companies already disclose such a metric.
qa_flags.response_pattern: CEO declines to give any current figure and instead responds twice with 'Come next week', deferring quantification to the Financial Analyst Day rather than answering on the spot.
